rows.Main Input: Spatial transcriptomics count matrix + spatial coordinates
rows.Main Use in This Topic: normalize spatial transcriptomics data by separating library-size effects from spatial biology
rows.Main Output: normalized expression matrix for downstream spatial analyses
rows.Closest Alternatives: scGIST is the only frozen cross-branch alternative; it selects targeted gene panels rather than normalizing measured expression.
rows.Key Difference: Models spatially structured library-size effects and biological signal directly, whereas the other frozen method is a pre-assay feature-selection tool.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed/DOI verify the Genome Biology SpaNorm method paper, and Bioconductor confirms package availability. Layer 2 synthesis: closest-alternative wording, resource burden, scale sensitivity, and signal-removal caveat.
rows.Best First Choice When: When the task is post-capture spatial-aware normalization and library-size effects may be spatially associated with biological domains.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When the task is selecting a fixed targeted gene panel before an imaging-based spatial transcriptomics experiment.
rows.Scientific-risk Caveat: Normalization can remove or attenuate biology if technical depth effects are not separable from real spatial structure; the direct paper evidence is method-local rather than an independent cross-method benchmark.

rows.Main Input: Single-cell expression data, cell labels or cell-type structure, prioritized gene sets, and a target panel size
rows.Main Use in This Topic: select genes for targeted spatial transcriptomics panels with prioritized biological or technical gene sets
rows.Main Output: selected gene panel for targeted spatial transcriptomics assays
rows.Closest Alternatives: SpaNorm is the only frozen cross-branch alternative; it normalizes measured spatial expression rather than selecting assay features.
rows.Key Difference: Optimizes a gene panel before targeted spatial measurement, whereas the other frozen method transforms observed spatial expression after data generation.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed/DOI verify the Genome Biology scGIST method paper, and the paper records GitHub and Zenodo code/data availability. Layer 2 synthesis: resource burden, scale sensitivity, and panel-transfer caveats.
rows.Best First Choice When: When the task is targeted spatial transcriptomics gene-panel design and the user needs prioritized gene sets or cell-type-discriminative feature selection.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When the task is normalizing an already measured whole-transcriptome or targeted spatial expression matrix.
rows.Scientific-risk Caveat: Panel performance can depend on reference data, labels, tissue context, panel-size constraints, and transfer to the target assay; the direct paper evidence is not an independent benchmark against SpaNorm because the tasks differ.
